// diagnostic

E0106

Redefining a built-in

What

Redefining a built-in

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Rename the declaration so it does not shadow a built-in.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0106: tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.stderr.

Error [E0106]: The name `Cache` is built in and can't be redefined
  --> tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:12:8
    |
 12 | struct Cache {
    |        ^^^^^
 Why: `Cache` is provided by the language itself
 Fix: Choose a different name for this struct
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0106

Error [E1102]: `cell` can't cross into a task because `Cell<Int>` isn't sendable
  --> tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:2:20
    |
  2 |     worker :: task {
    |                    ^
 Why: `Cell` owns thread-local state and must stay on the thread that created it; tasks and channels move owned values between threads
 Fix: Create the `Cell<T>` inside the task, or use `Shared<T>` for synchronized state
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1102

Error [E0120]: `cell` was not moved here, so it cannot be taken with the move marker `^`
  --> tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:3:14
    |
  3 |         _ :: cell
    |              ^^^^
 Why: This function has read access only and does not own the value
 Fix: Copy it instead: `_ :: ~cell`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0120

Error [E1102]: `Cell`<Int> cannot be stored in `Shared<T>`
  --> tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:9:17
    |
  9 |     _ :: shared cell
    |                 ^^^^
 Why: A Cell and its guards own one-thread borrow state; wrapping that state does not make it synchronized
 Fix: Store the value itself in `Shared<T>`, then read and write its fields directly
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1102

Error [E0119]: There's no type called `Cache`
  --> tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:16:31
    |
 16 | fn cross_shared_nested(cache: Cache) {
    |                               ^^^^^
 Why: The types are `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, and `String` (plus types you define)
 Fix: Check the spelling, or define the struct or enum first
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0119
